title: 七类预训练数据构建范式对比

claims.claim: The T5 paper introduces C4 as a cleaned Common Crawl corpus and discusses filtering decisions including deduplication and removal of incomplete or noisy content.
claims.locator: T5 paper; C4 dataset construction discussion
claims.notes: The chapter intentionally avoids unsupported single-number claims about C4 size or a universal set of cleaning rules.

claims.claim: CCNet combines document deduplication and language identification with language-model perplexity filtering toward high-quality reference sources such as Wikipedia.
claims.notes: Perplexity is a source-conditioned signal, not a universal quality score across domains and languages.

claims.claim: The Pile paper describes an 825 GiB English text corpus composed of 22 datasets.
claims.notes: The corpus is heterogeneous; size and source count do not imply uniform license or quality across subsets.

claims.claim: The RefinedWeb paper reports extracting five trillion tokens from Common Crawl and publicly releasing a 600-billion-token extract.
claims.notes: Attribute figures and performance claims to the paper's own setup and do not generalize its result to every model or task.

claims.claim: FineWeb is described as a 15-trillion-token dataset from 96 Common Crawl snapshots, and FineWeb-Edu as a 1.3-trillion-token educational subset.
claims.notes: FineWeb-Edu's educational-quality signal is task-specific and should not be treated as a universal truth label.

claims.claim: The Dolma paper describes a three-trillion-token English corpus from web, scientific papers, code, public-domain books, social media and encyclopedic materials.
claims.notes: Distinguish the corpus paper from later dataset snapshots and the separately versioned toolkit.

claims.claim: The FLUX preprint reports 32.14% MMLU for a 3B model trained on 60B tokens, compared with 31.98% for DCLM and 29.88% for FineWeb in its described experiment.
claims.notes: This is an author-reported result in a 2026 arXiv preprint and is valid only within the paper's experimental setup; it is not a cross-paper leaderboard or settled consensus.

claims.claim: Cross-paper dataset comparisons should control model, token budget, tokenizer, data snapshots, benchmark version and decontamination protocol.
claims.locator: Tutorial comparability checklist; FLUX reports a paper-specific controlled comparison
claims.notes: This is a methodological recommendation for fair comparison, not a formula or result attributed to a single cited paper.
